output.brief: The jump in chilled write-offs is mostly caused by our own night receiving, not by Haverlow. Haverlow's trailer telematics show product at 2.4–3.5°C when the doors open, and the trailers were empty by about 23:00–23:40. Our system only confirms receipt, and records the probe reading, at 02:30–03:20. In between, pallets sit in unrefrigerated dock lanes at 15–17°C. Since the night team was cut from six to four on 27 July, median dock-to-chamber time rose from 44 minutes to about 3h52. Night write-offs rose from 0.6% to 2.9% for every supplier, while day shift stayed flat. The chambers held temperature. So the chargeback and the volume shift would penalise the wrong party, and they would leave the cause in place. Next step: restore night receiving staffing, or otherwise fix the dock flow, and set a maximum dock-to-chamber time monitored weekly. Probe on unload, not at receipt confirmation. Do not drop the probe check. Separately, sample Corriebank's claims, because part of the credit rise may be self-certified over-claiming. I'm confident on the main cause. The credit question is still open.
